figure: FIGURE 7.5 (KV cache size vs context length, by attention geometry)
issue: Caption states the GQA FP16 line reaches the ~436 GB KV budget 'only at ~132M tokens'. Recomputation from the book's own numbers gives ~1.32M tokens, not 132M — a 100x error. The figure itself contradicts the caption: the GQA FP16 line is still below the 436 GB dashed budget line at the right edge of the plot (x = 1000K = 1M tokens), where 0.33 MB/token x 1e6 = ~330 GB.
evidence: Caption: 'the GQA FP16 line reaches that budget only at ~132M tokens'. Recompute: 436 GB / 0.33 MB/token = 436e9 / 3.3e5 = 1.321e6 tokens = ~1.32M tokens. Cross-check against the plotted line: at 1M tokens the GQA FP16 series sits at ~330 GB, i.e. below the 436 GB budget line, so the budget cannot be reached at 132K or 132M; it is reached at ~1.32M. The same caption's other arithmetic is correct (2.62 MB/token x 128K = ~335 GB; 2.62 MB/token x 9.5K = 24.9 GB), so the error is localized to this one token count.
acceptance_test: Replace '~132M tokens' with '~1.32M tokens' and re-verify by recomputing 436 GB / 0.33 MB/token; confirm the printed value equals 1.32e6 +/- 0.01e6. If the intended figure was 132K, correct the divisor (0.33 MB/token x 132K = 43.6 GB, which does not reach the budget) — i.e. the number must be re-derived, not merely re-spelled.

issue: The legend entry 'full-MHA FP16 (raw byte-halving, 50%)' labels the byte-halved (8-bit) series as FP16, while the corresponding GQA series is correctly labelled 'GQA FP8 (raw byte-halving, 50%)'. As drawn, the legend contains two series labelled FP16 with different values, and a reader could conclude the book measures two distinct FP16 KV footprints.
evidence: Legend: 'full-MHA FP16 (bound, ~2.62 MB/tok)' (red), 'full-MHA FP16 (raw byte-halving, 50%)' (orange), 'GQA FP16 (~0.33 MB/tok)' (blue), 'GQA FP8 (raw byte-halving, 50%)' (green). Caption: 'FP16 = 2.62 MB/token, FP8/8-bit = 1.31' and 'The FP8 value is raw byte-halving (50% of FP16)'. The orange series therefore represents 1.31 MB/token, i.e. FP8, not FP16.
acceptance_test: Rename the orange legend entry to 'full-MHA FP8 (raw byte-halving of FP16, 50%)' and confirm the legend contains exactly one FP16 series per attention geometry, with the byte-halved series labelled FP8 in both geometries.

issue: The annotation '9.5K x 3.1 GB (GQA FP16)' uses a multiplication sign where a mapping is meant, and the parallel annotation '9.5K = 24.9 GB (FP16 bound)' uses '='. The two annotations for the same x-position are therefore written in two different, one of them wrong, relations.
evidence: Rendered annotations: '9.5K = 24.9 GB (FP16 bound)' and '9.5K x 3.1 GB (GQA FP16)'. Values check out: 2.62 MB x 9,500 = 24.9 GB; 0.33 MB x 9,500 = 3.1 GB.
acceptance_test: Rewrite both annotations with a single consistent relation (e.g. '9.5K -> 24.9 GB (full-MHA FP16)' and '9.5K -> 3.1 GB (GQA FP16)') and confirm the arithmetic still matches 2.62 and 0.33 MB/token.

figure: Figure 7.6 — Inference vs fine-tuning memory floor
issue: The QLoRA footnote annotation states 'KV 24 GB' but Figures 7.7 (PDF 149) and 7.8 (PDF 151) both use '24.9 GB' for the same 9.5K-context FP16 KV on the same 70B full-MHA model. If the QLoRA scenario uses the same 9.5K max context as the inference bar (which yields ~165 GB = 140 + 24.9), the KV should be ~24.9 GB, not 24 GB. With KV = 24.9, the QLoRA total would be 35 + 24.9 + 1 = 60.9 ≈ 61 GB, not the printed ~60 GB. The 1 GB discrepancy suggests either (a) 24.9 was incorrectly rounded down to 24, or (b) the QLoRA scenario silently uses the 9.2K canonical context (9,200 × 2.62 MB ≈ 24.1 GB) while the inference bar uses 9.5K — but the figure does not state different context lengths per scenario.
evidence: Figure 7.6 footnote: 'QLoRA: 4-bit (NF4) base 35 GB + KV 24 GB + LoRA adapters/optimizer ~1 GB.' Bar label: '~60 GB.' 35 + 24 + 1 = 60 (internally consistent with 24). Figure 7.7 caption: '24.9 GB/request max-FP16 KV (9.5K max context).' Figure 7.8: 'KV 24.9 GB' at 9.5K. Inference bar in 7.6: ~165 GB = 140 + 24.9 (implies 9.5K).
acceptance_test: Decide whether all three scenarios in Figure 7.6 use the same context length. If 9.5K: change QLoRA KV to '24.9 GB' and total to '~61 GB' (or '~60–61 GB'). If 9.2K: add an explicit context annotation to the QLoRA footnote (e.g., 'KV ~24 GB at 9.2K canonical'). Confirm the bar height and label are updated to match. Verify no downstream text references '~60 GB' for QLoRA that would also need updating.

issue: The horizontal reference lines for 2xH100, 8xH100, and 1xH100 are distinguished only by subtle dash patterns (dashed, dash-dot, dotted) and are not reliably distinguishable in grayscale at print size.

figure: FIGURE 7.7 — Concurrency budget — one 8×H100 host, 640 GB pool
issue: The displayed equation inside the figure uses '+' where the arithmetic requires division: it reads '≈ 436 GB + 24.9 GB = 17.5 → ~17 requests'. As printed this is false (436 + 24.9 = 460.9, not 17.5). The line immediately above it ('in-flight = KV budget ÷ KV per request') and the caption ('KV budget ÷ per-request KV price sets concurrency') both use division, so the figure contradicts its own prose and caption.
evidence: Rendered page 129 (PDF 149): equation line reads '≈ 436 GB + 24.9 GB = 17.5 → ~17 requests'; the preceding line reads 'in-flight = KV budget ÷ KV per request'; caption reads 'KV budget ÷ per-request KV price sets concurrency — at 24.9 GB/request max-fit is KV'. Independent recomputation: 436 GB ÷ 24.9 GB/request = 17.51 → ~17 requests (matches the printed result 17.5); 436 + 24.9 = 460.9 GB, which cannot equal 17.5. The glyph is a plus sign with a visible vertical stroke, not a division sign with dots above/below.
acceptance_test: In the built PDF at 300 dpi the operator between '436 GB' and '24.9 GB' must be '÷' (division sign), and the line must read '≈ 436 GB ÷ 24.9 GB = 17.5 → ~17 requests'. Verify by OCR/visual inspection at 300 dpi, not at 150 dpi.

issue: The caption says the KV cache is 'consuming the fixed ~436 GB KV budget,' but the 128K bar shows only 335 GB of KV, leaving 101 GB of the stated budget unused. The wording implies the KV block fills the budget, while the drawing correctly shows it does not.
evidence: The 128K bar's orange KV segment is labeled 'KV 335 GB' and the total used is 539 GB. The fixed KV budget is stated as ~436 GB. 436 - 335 = 101 GB. The caption's phrase 'consuming the fixed ~436 GB KV budget' is therefore imprecise for the 128K case.
acceptance_test: Revise the caption to say the KV cache 'draws from' or 'is bounded by' the ~436 GB budget, and explicitly note that at 128K one request uses 335 GB, leaving 101 GB stranded because a second 335 GB request cannot fit.

figure: FIGURE 7.8 — Memory Tetris: how the 8×H100 host (640 GB) fills with context
issue: The figure note 'Bar heights are not to scale (GB)' contradicts the drawing: the three bars are rendered approximately in proportion to their labelled totals (229 / 288 / 539 GB), so a reader who trusts the note will misread the visual as schematic when it is in fact quantitative — and a reader who trusts the drawing will be misled by the note into distrusting a correct proportionality.
evidence: Rendered page 131 (PDF 131): bar labels '9.5K context = 229 GB used', '32K context = 288 GB used', '128K context = 539 GB used'. Measured bar heights in the 150 dpi render are approximately 55 px, 80 px and 155 px from a common baseline, i.e. ratios 0.35 / 0.52 / 1.00 against the labelled ratios 0.425 / 0.534 / 1.00 — proportional to within roughly 8%, not schematic. The note directly below the legend reads 'Bar heights are not to scale (GB).'
acceptance_test: Choose one and make it true: (a) keep the proportional bars and replace the note with 'No y-axis scale is shown; all values are labelled in GB', or (b) keep the note and redraw the bars so the proportionality is visibly broken. The chosen wording must not assert a property the drawing contradicts.

figure: FIGURE 7.8 — Memory Tetris: how the 8×H100 host (640 GB) fills with context
issue: The figure title 'how the 8×H100 host (640 GB) fills with context' overstates what the figure shows: even at 128K context the host is only 539/640 GB used, i.e. it never fills. The title invites the reader to look for a saturation event that the figure does not contain, and it slightly pre-empts the caption's own point that the KV budget is the binding constraint.
evidence: Rendered page 151 (PDF 151): title 'Memory Tetris: how the 8×H100 host (640 GB) fills with context'; bar labels '9.5K context = 229 GB used', '32K context = 288 GB used', '128K context = 539 GB used'; the 640 GB rule is drawn above all three bars with visible headroom in every case.
acceptance_test: Retitle to something the figure supports, e.g. 'Memory Tetris: how the 8×H100 host (640 GB) fills with context — and where it stops filling', or 'Memory Tetris: KV growth inside the 8×H100 host (640 GB)', and ensure the title does not assert saturation.
